items.stem: In ITIL/ITSM terms, what is the primary goal of incident management?

options.text: Restore normal service operation as quickly as possible
options.rationale: Correct: incident management focuses on rapid restoration of service, not root cause.

options.text: Find and remove the root cause of recurring issues
options.rationale: That is the goal of problem management, not incident management.

items.explanation: Correct: incident management focuses on rapid restoration of service, not root cause.

items.stem: Which ServiceNow capability defines and tracks the time targets for resolving a record?

options.rationale: Correct: SLA definitions set and measure time targets against schedules and conditions.
Business rules run logic on database operations, not SLA tracking specifically.
Catalog items are requestable services, not time targets.
Assignment rules route records; they do not track time targets.

items.explanation: Correct: SLA definitions set and measure time targets against schedules and conditions.

items.stem: Which TWO are typically pre-approved and low-risk in change management?

options.rationale: Correct: standard changes are pre-authorised, low-risk and repeatable.

options.text: Routine password-reset-type changes following an approved model
options.rationale: Correct: changes following an approved standard model skip full CAB review.

options.text: Emergency changes to fix a major outage
options.rationale: Emergency changes are high-urgency and need expedited (not pre-) approval.
Large, high-risk changes require full assessment and CAB.
Untested changes carry risk and are not pre-approved.

items.explanation: Correct: standard changes are pre-authorised, low-risk and repeatable.
